summary: Proposes a simple file format for storing black-and-white bitmaps, with a short header giving the width and number of lines. It was meant for short-term storage and passing data between closely coupled programs.

eli5.summary: A picture made of tiny black or white squares can be saved as a list of ones and zeros. This memo says how to lay that list out in a file.

questions: simple one bit per pixel file format
how to store black and white images
subtitle: A simple format for storing black-and-white pictures as files of bits.

tldr.problem: Programs needed a simple, compact way to store and exchange black-and-white bitmap images.
tldr.mechanism: The file format consists of a 10-octet header (width, height, and x/y pixel spacing), followed by the bitmap data stored in 8-bit bytes with pixels packed left-to-right and lines top-to-bottom, padded to octet boundaries.
tldr.outcome: A minimal format suitable for short-term storage and data interchange between tightly coupled programs on the same system.

today: RFC 797 describes a minimal format intended for short-term use. While simple bitmap formats remain useful for interchange, modern image applications use more sophisticated formats like PNG, BMP, and TIFF that support additional features and compression.

sections.title: File Structure Overview
sections.content: RFC 797 proposes a simple format for storing one-bit-per-pixel (monochrome) bitmaps in files. The RFC emphasizes that this format is intended for short-term storage and interchange between closely coupled programs, not as a universal image format. Each file begins with a 10-octet header followed by the bitmap data.
sections.eli5: This is a quick and simple way to save a black-and-white picture when programs on the same computer need to share it.

sections.title: Header and Bitmap Layout
sections.content: The header consists of: Width (octets 1–4, most significant octet first), Height (octets 5–8), X increment (octet 9), and Y increment (octet 10). The X and Y increment fields specify how much space is between pixels (normally both are 1, but different values allow for different scan modes, such as from facsimile machines). The bitmap data follows immediately, with each scan line stored from left to right and all lines from top to bottom. Each line must end on an octet boundary; if the width is not divisible by 8, the remainder of the last octet is filled with zero bits.
sections.eli5: The first 10 bytes say 'width is X, height is Y, skip X pixels at a time, skip Y lines at a time.' Then come the picture bytes.

sections.title: Facsimile Machine Support
sections.content: The RFC notes that bitmaps from the Rapicom 450 facsimile machine (subject of RFC 798) can be in different modes. In fine-detail mode, the x-increment and y-increment are both 1. In quality mode, x-increment is 1 and y-increment is 2 (meaning each scan line should be displayed twice on playback). In express mode, x-increment is 1 and y-increment is 3 (each line displayed three times). This flexibility allows fax data to be stored in a uniform bitmap format while preserving the original scan resolution information.
sections.eli5: A fax machine might send every line of a picture, or every other line, or every third line. The header numbers tell the display whether to repeat lines when showing the picture.

fields.name: Width byte 1
fields.desc: Most significant byte of image width.
